title: Variables and controlled experiments in physics
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:41Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank card covers controlled and confounding variables in psychology but not the independent and dependent variable link or cause and effect, so adapting it would need added content rather than small changes.

draft.title: Variables and controlled experiments
card: the quantity the experimenter deliberately changes. There should be only one in a test.
the quantity that is measured to see how it responds to the change.
all other quantities that could affect the result. They are kept the same, so they cannot explain any change in the dependent variable.

If only the independent variable changes and the dependent variable changes with it, the investigation supports a cause and effect link. If a second quantity also changes, the cause cannot be pinned down.
draft.remember: Change one thing, measure the response, and hold everything else the same.

a.q: Why must the controlled variables be kept constant in an investigation?
opts: So they cannot explain a change in the dependent variable
So the independent variable stays the same in every trial
So the dependent variable does not change at all
So the measurements need no repeats
a.why: If a controlled variable also changed, it could be the real cause of the change in the dependent variable. Keeping them constant removes that doubt. The independent variable is the one that is deliberately changed, so it does not stay the same.
a.clue: Think about what else could cause the change you see.

b.q: Priya rolls a trolley down a ramp and times it. She raises the ramp to different heights to see how ramp height affects the trolley's final speed. Which quantity is a controlled variable?
opts: The final speed of the trolley
The cause of the speed change
b.why: The trolley's mass could affect the result, so it must be kept the same in every run. Ramp height is the independent variable because Priya changes it. Final speed is the dependent variable because she measures it.
b.clue: Which quantity is neither changed on purpose nor measured as the result?

a.best: So they cannot explain a change in the dependent variable

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clearly correct answer that matches the card. The explanations are accurate and consistent with it.
